generator.params.note: Hand-set to give a plausible Douglas-fir: annual whorls of about five branches, upper branches swept up and lower ones level to drooping with upturned tips, a stiff leader, foliage kept about six years, height near 35 m at 50 years on a good site. Spray area matched to the drawn needle sprays. Not fitted to data. Cones (plant forms F3): 5 to 10 cm hang, with three-pointed bracts between the scales; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured.

allometry.note: Rough heights and diameters for a well-stocked western Washington stand, from general forestry knowledge. Replace with a published yield or site-index table before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye. Needles stand all round the twigs (bottlebrush), unlike the flat sprays of true firs and cedars; bark thick and furrowed with a modest flare. Needle shoots (plant roadmap P4): needles 2 to 3 cm long and 1 to 1.5 mm wide, so a needle 0.05 as wide as it is long (`width`), from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Bark pattern (plant roadmap P4, `bark_pattern`): smooth with resin blisters when young, then very thick and deeply furrowed into dark brown ridges; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

generator.program.note: The program the spec's authors chose to grow this form.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).
